newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian stocks jump as cenbank woos investors.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian stocks jump as cenbank woos investors.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index closed two percent higher on Friday as the market welcomed the decision by the Bank of Slovenia to ease rules for those who buy securities for a period of more than seven years.
The SBI index jumped 2.01 percent or 24.91 points to 1,262.5, marking up gains for the seventh day in a row.
"Prices went up because of the central bank's decree, but I think the rise is likely to stabilise over the next week," said Tone Cerne, a trader at brokerage BPH.
He added that foreign investors were unlikely to rush in before they could fully examine the decree.
Banks said the new decree would enable them to reduce costs of the fiduciary accounts significantly in cases of long-term purchases, but gave no estimate of the new costs.

International investors have stayed away from the Slovenian market since February when the central bank ruled that foreigners must open fiduciary accounts at one of 14 fully licensed banks in order to trade in securities.
Since then the Ljubljana bourse turnover has dropped to a tenth of its previous level, while the blue chip index has fallen over 23 percent.

"We have to wait until July 15 when we will see what happens to our EU membership, if the news is good the index could jump by some 20 percent in a week or two, if not it could be the other way around," Cerne said.
The association agreement that was signed in June last year still needs to be ratified by Slovenia's parliament and by most EU parliaments before being enforced.
Overall 11 shares rose, five fell and 13 were untraded. Turnover jumped to 103.6 million tolars from 71.8 million
Food maker Droga was the most active share, easing 1.03 percent to 28,000 tolars on volume of 2,338 shares for total turnover of 63.6 million tolars.
Preferred shares of trading firm Kovinotehna were the top gainers, jumping 8.97 percent to 425 tolars on volume of 200 shares.
Traders said the rise was a technical rebound after a similar loss over the last two trading sessions.
Financial consultancy Finmedia led decliners, falling 7.02 percent to 11,120 tolars on volume of six shares only.
Bank Dolenjska jumped 7.69 percent to 14,000 tolars on volume of 194 shares.
Bank Probanka rose 3.46 percent to 19,150 tolars on volume of 167 shares.
Traders said both shares rose following a decision of the Bank of Slovenia to allow Daiwa Europe to buy 2.94 percent of bank Probanka and 3.51 percent of Dolenjska banka.
